title: Landscaping Software: 6 Tools by Job Type and Price
html:
Landscaping software has to do three jobs: price the work, schedule the crew and get paid. Small crews start with a scheduling and invoicing app, and larger firms add estimating and job costing. Add landscaping CRM automation once follow-ups slip. Published prices here run from $29 to $648 a month, and two vendors publish none.

Landscaping software earns its price when a crew stops losing money on jobs it priced by feel. A mowing route, a patio build and a spring cleanup each need different pricing and a different kind of tracking. This guide compares six tools by job type, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Landscaping is seasonal. Work piles up in spring, and a tool you need in May may sit idle in January. So the guide flags what each vendor says about plans and add-ons.

Which landscaping software suits a small crew?

Jobber and Service Fusion are the two apps a mowing or maintenance crew compares first. Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments.

  • Jobber: a field service app with scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. The Core plan for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and card processing is 2.9% plus 30 cents.
  • Service Fusion: customer management, estimates, scheduling, dispatching, invoicing and payment processing. Starter is $208 a month billed annually or $245 billed monthly, with unlimited users on every plan and month to month terms. Limit: add-ons such as GPS fleet tracking are listed without prices.

The split is crew size. Jobber Core fits an owner who runs one route, since every extra mower operator adds a $29 seat. Service Fusion has no seat math, so a crew that grows from four to nine in spring pays the same price.

Check the billing term too. Jobber lists no commitment, one year and annual options, so the same plan has three prices. Service Fusion lists annual and monthly prices. Compare the same term across vendors before you rank them.

Seasonal crews feel that difference. If you hire ten people for six months, a per-user plan swells with the headcount. Ask each vendor whether you can drop users in winter and what that does to your bill.

Which landscaping software handles estimating and job costing?

LMN and Arborgold are built for landscape and lawn firms that need budgets, job costing and multi-day scheduling, not just a calendar.

Job costing is what separates these from a calendar app. It compares the hours and materials you priced with what the job used. Without it, a patio build that runs two days over still looks like a win on the invoice.

LMN is the larger commitment. A $297 monthly plan plus an onboarding fee only pays off if the owner will keep a budget and use it. Arborgold lists a lower starting price, so ask what the real plan costs for your crew size.

Which landscaping software covers design and CRM?

DynaScape and SynkedUP serve firms that sell design work or want lead intake tied to estimating.

Design software matters for firms that sell installs. A to-scale plan with a plant list closes a bigger job than a sketch on a napkin. A mowing company that never draws plans would be paying for features it never opens.

SynkedUP is a closer fit for a firm that wants lead intake and estimating in one place. Ask for a demo that uses your own price list, since a template estimate hides how the tool handles your real jobs.

How do the six landscaping software tools compare?

The table puts the published facts side by side so you can see where each tool starts and where it stops.

ToolPublished entry priceBuilt forMain limit
Jobber$29 a month billed annually, $49 with no commitmentSmall crewsExtra users cost $29 a month
Service Fusion$208 a month billed annuallyGrowing crewsAdd-on prices not shown
LMN$297 a month billed monthlyEstimating and budgetsOne-time onboarding fee
ArborgoldFrom $119 a monthEstimating and schedulingPlan details not shown
DynaScapeRequest a quoteDesign and CADNo published price
SynkedUPNot publishedCRM and estimatingNo published price

Source: each vendor's own pages, read in November 2026. Prices exclude tax, card processing fees and onboarding fees.

Read the table by business type. Mowing and maintenance points to Jobber or Service Fusion. Design-build points to DynaScape. A firm with budgets and many crews points to LMN, Arborgold or SynkedUP.

Which landscaping software features matter most?

Five features decide whether a landscaping tool earns its price: recurring jobs, crew time tracking, estimating templates, job costing and photo records.

  • Recurring jobs: a weekly mow or a monthly fertilizer visit should repeat and invoice itself, so the office does not rebuild the route each week.
  • Crew time tracking: punch-in data shows where labor goes, which is the biggest cost on most jobs.
  • Estimating templates: a saved template for a mulch job or a paver patio keeps bids consistent between estimators.
  • Job costing: it compares the bid with actual hours and materials. LMN lists it on Professional, and Arborgold lists it on its landscaping page.
  • Photo records: before and after photos settle disputes and double as proof of work for your website.

You may not need all five on day one. A mowing company can skip estimating templates, and a design-build firm can skip recurring jobs. Rank the five by where you lose money today, then match tools to the top two.

What should a landscaper test during a software trial?

Test the moments that cost money in this trade: a recurring route, a rained-out day and a multi-day install. A clean demo job shows none of those.

  1. Build a recurring route. Set weekly visits for twenty properties and check that the schedule repeats without manual edits.
  2. Move a rained-out day. Push a day of jobs forward and see whether customers are told.
  3. Price a multi-day install. Add labor, materials and equipment, then compare the total with your last real bid.
  4. Log time on a phone. Have a crew lead punch in and out from the truck.
  5. Send an invoice. Turn a finished job into an invoice and take a card payment.

Test in your busy month if you can. A tool that feels fine in January can buckle when one hundred jobs arrive in April. Ask the vendor how many properties and crews a plan comfortably holds.

Give the trial to a crew lead as well as the owner. The person who rides the truck finds clumsy screens first, and the crew has to use the tool every day.

What does a landscaping software stack cost per month?

A small landscaping stack costs $29 to $297 a month for the core app, using only the published prices above. Add the extras that fit your work.

  • Solo mowing route: Jobber Core at $29 a month billed annually, plus a free Google Business Profile.
  • Crew of five or more: Service Fusion Starter at $208 a month billed annually covers unlimited users.
  • Estimating and budgets: LMN Starter at $297 a month billed monthly, plus the onboarding fee. Professional is $648.
  • Design-build firm: DynaScape or SynkedUP by quote.

These figures cover the software only. Card processing, onboarding and add-ons sit on top, and your website still needs a home.

Compare the stack with one average job. If a tool costs less than a single install a month and saves an hour a day, it pays for itself. Cancel plans in winter if the vendor allows it.

What does landscaping software not do?

Landscaping software runs the work after a customer says yes. It does not bring in requests, so a full schedule still depends on search, maps and reviews.

  • Google Business Profile: the free listing that puts a landscaping company on Google Maps. Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it needs fresh project photos and review replies to rank near the top.

How do you choose landscaping software?

Choose landscaping software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it handle recurring routes, multi-day installs and rain delays, and does it cost jobs against the bid?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users, onboarding and card fees, then compare the total with one average job.

Setup effort: can one person import clients, build a price list and train the crew before the season starts?

A solo mower can run on Jobber Core and a free Google Business Profile. A growing crew fits Service Fusion. A firm that bids installs should price LMN or Arborgold against a quote from DynaScape or SynkedUP.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from landscaping Google Ads and Google Local Services Ads bring requests in.

What is the best landscaping software for a small crew?

There is no single best, because it depends on crew size and job type. Jobber Core at $29 a month billed annually suits a solo route. Service Fusion offers unlimited users from $208 a month billed annually. LMN suits firms that need budgets and job costing.

How much does landscaping software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $29 a month for Jobber Core, billed annually, to $648 a month for LMN Professional. Arborgold lists plans from $119. Onboarding and card fees cost extra.

Do landscapers need job costing software?

Job costing matters when you bid installs, because it compares the hours and materials you priced with what the job used. Mowing routes need it less. LMN lists real-time job costing on Professional, and Arborgold lists job costing on its landscaping page.

Is there free landscaping software?

The vendors in this guide sell paid plans, so none is free to run a business on. Jobber and Service Fusion list plans from a monthly price. A shared calendar and a spreadsheet cost nothing, but they lack invoicing, routes and customer history.

Can landscaping software get me more customers?

No. Landscaping software organizes work after a customer says yes. New requests come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A free Google Business Profile, a site with project photos and paid search put your number in front of homeowners first.

When should a landscaping company move to bigger software?

Move up when you run several crews, bid multi-day installs or lose money on jobs you cannot explain. Until then a lighter app is cheaper and easier to learn. Request quotes from LMN, Arborgold or SynkedUP only when those needs are real.
